title: A Path Through the Waypoints: Corners, Smooth Curves, and the Loop That Uneven Spacing Makes

questions.question: A robot follows straight lines between four waypoints on a square route. How sharp is the turn at a corner, in one step?
questions.explanation: The whole angle in a single step, which no machine can follow. A curve through the same waypoints turned at most 10.9 degrees in a step.

questions.question: What does the alpha of a Catmull-Rom curve set?
options: How the curve is timed along the way
questions.explanation: 0 gives every waypoint the same time, 0.5 the square root of the distance, 1 the distance. The curve passes through every waypoint whatever alpha is.

questions.question: Waypoints spaced 10, 1 and 14.1. What is the sharpest turn in one step with alpha 0 and with alpha 0.5?
questions.explanation: Uniform timing makes the curve turn back on itself. Chordal timing gave 8.7 degrees.

questions.question: Why does uniform timing loop on uneven waypoints?
options: Every segment gets the same time
questions.explanation: The short step has to be crossed as slowly as the long runs and the curve rushes through it and turns back. Timing by distance fixes it.

questions.question: What happens at a waypoint that is repeated?
options: It is skipped silently with a warning
A distance of zero gives a time interval of zero and a division by it
questions.explanation: Repeated waypoints are taken once and the curve function goes straight on a zero interval. Waypoints on a line with the last repeated stayed exactly on it.

questions.question: What does the curve not do?
options: Say anything about speed, avoid obstacles between waypoints, or help when the waypoints are noisy and the robot only needs to pass near them
questions.explanation: A velocity profile is lesson 14-06's job.
